Q230.L1t: A combine harvester is a machine that cuts, threshes and cleans grain crops in a single pass through the field.
Q230.L2t: Threshing in a combine separates the grain from the stalks and husks using rotating drums or rotors working against a concave.
Q230.L3t: Behind the threshing cylinder, a rotating bar-equipped drum strips remaining grain from the straw and pushes the straw out of the machine, whereas seed-metering plates and furrow-cutting tools belong to planting equipment, not harvesting.
Q230.L4t: The beater is the component that belongs to a farm combine.
Q230.L2f: Combine harvesters were first developed in the 1990s and have always been powered by animals pulling them across the field.
Q230.L3f: A seed plate is a metering disc inside the combine's threshing system that regulates how much grain passes from the cylinder to the cleaning shoe.
Q230.L4f: The seed plate is the part that belongs to a farm combine.

Q527.L1t: Mental disorders are conditions affecting mood, thinking and behavior, and the World Health Organization tracks their global burden through population surveys.
Q527.L2t: Global epidemiological estimates group mental disorders into categories such as mood, anxiety, psychotic and substance use disorders, with prevalence varying by region and by how cases are defined.
Q527.L3t: Global burden estimates show that conditions marked by excessive fear and worry affect several hundred million people worldwide, far more than any of the severe mood-swing or psychotic conditions, which each affect only tens of millions.
Q527.L4t: Anxiety disorders are the most prevalent mental disorders in the world.
Q527.L2f: Surveys of mental disorders have found that prevalence is identical in every country and age group, with no variation by region or definition.
Q527.L3f: Global burden estimates show that bipolar disorder affects more people worldwide than any other mental disorder, outnumbering anxiety, depression and substance use conditions combined.
Q527.L4f: Bipolar disorder is the most prevalent mental disorder in the world.

Q553.L1t: Writing can be classified into broad types according to the author's purpose, such as informing, persuading, describing or telling a story.
Q553.L2t: The passage is written in the first person and recalls a childhood event from the winter of 1975 together with its long-lasting effects on the speaker.
Q553.L3t: The excerpt recounts a specific past event in sequence, with a first-person character, a setting, and a moment that shapes the character's life, which are the features of story-telling writing rather than of explaining facts.
Q553.L4t: The excerpt is an example of narrative writing.
Q553.L2f: The passage is taken from a technical manual about winter weather conditions and was written to teach readers how frozen creeks form.
Q553.L3f: The excerpt is built mainly to present factual information and explain a subject to readers, such as the history of the winter of 1975, without any character or personal event.
Q553.L4f: The excerpt is an example of informative writing.
